pages.text: The $(item)Blueprint Repository$() is your blueprint library. It starts $(l)empty$(): you fill it by depositing the discs you find and scan, then re-burn any catalogued build onto a fresh disc whenever you need a copy.$(br2)Right-click it to open the browser: catalogued builds on the left, details on the right.

pages.title: Depositing Discs
pages.text: Drop a $(l)written$() Blueprint Disc into the input slot and press $(l)Deposit Disc$(). The build is catalogued into the library and the disc is consumed.$(br2)Once catalogued you can re-burn as many copies as you like, and it stays until somebody $(l)removes$() it on purpose.

pages.title: Duplicates Recycle
pages.text: Deposit a disc the library $(l)already has$() and it won't be wasted: the disc is wiped and handed back as a $(item)Blank Blueprint Disc$() you can reuse.$(br2)$(l)Locked$() discs are protected: a duplicate locked disc is left untouched instead of being recycled.$(br2)A re-deposit never rewrites the catalogued entry: it keeps its name and its original depositor.

pages.title: STL to GCODE
pages.text: Select a build in the list, drop a $(item)Blank Blueprint Disc$() into the input slot, and press $(l)STL to GCODE$() to burn a fresh written disc.$(br2)Burned copies keep the original's $(l)official$() or $(l)player-scan$() status, so the Resin anti-dupe rule still holds.

pages.title: Renaming Scans
pages.text: The $(item)Structure Scanner$() names a capture after where you stood: $(o)Scan @ 307,70,10$(). Useless once you've deposited a few.$(br2)Select a scan and a $(l)rename$() field appears under its details. Type a name, press $(l)Set$() (or Enter). The new title sticks in the library $(l)and$() in the stored blueprint, so a disc you burn later carries it too.$(br2)$(l)Player scans only$(). Official builds keep their shipped names - they are content, and on a shared library one edit would retitle the build for the whole server.$(br2)Names cap at $(l)48$() characters; formatting codes and line breaks are stripped.

pages.title: Removing a Scan
pages.text: Deposited something by mistake? Select it and press $(l)Del$() $(o)twice$() - the button arms on the first click and reads $(l)Sure?$() for five seconds.$(br2)$(li)Whoever $(l)deposited$() it can remove it$(li)$(l)Operators$() can remove anything$(li)$(l)Official$() builds can't be removed at all$(br2)The default library is shared, so an open button would let anyone wipe other players' contributions.$(br2)Removal takes the $(l)catalogue entry only$(), never the blueprint file: a disc burned earlier still prints, and re-depositing it restores the entry.$(br2)Entries catalogued before removal existed have no recorded depositor, so those are $(l)operator-only$().

pages.title: Shared or Personal
pages.text: By default a repository is a $(l)shared, world-level$() library: everyone's deposits pool together, every repository block sees the same catalogue, and breaking a block never loses it.$(br2)Server admins can flip $(l)blueprintRepositoryIsShared$() to $(l)false$() in the config for $(l)personal$() per-player libraries instead.
The Blueprint Repository. One per base is plenty: it's the home for every build you collect.
